summary: The aspect of a terrain surface
description:
Compute the aspect (in radians, from due North) of elevation data.

The aspect is the direction that the slope faces (the downslope direction), measured **clockwise from north**, from 0 to 2π: a slope that faces north gives 0, east π/2, south π and west 3π/2. This is the convention of GDAL `gdaldem aspect`, in radians.

The gradients use central differences with the pixel size of the data cube in metres. For a geographic CRS (for example EPSG:4326), the pixel size in degrees is converted to metres on a sphere. For best results, resample the elevation to a projected grid first (for example with `resample_cube_spatial`).

The result keeps the grid of the input (same size and bounds). The pixels on the 1-pixel border, and the pixels next to a no-data value, are no-data.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A raster data cube with n bands containing elevation data, in metres.

returns.description: A data cube with n bands named after the n bands in the input data cube, suffixed with `_aspect`. Each band contains the computed aspect values (in radians, clockwise from due North). In case the surface is flat, the NaN value is used (since there is no direction of the gradient).
